body: We need to make it crash somehow to figure out whats holding the lock. My money is on Windows firewall blocking socket writes indefinately.

Tricky... we lost the "monitor" process (SyncTrayor) when that dies, so we won't be able to capture output even if we do get it to crash.

I can probably code up something to kill Syncthing if it does die, but I'm not sure how to kill it in such a way that it will produce the output you need, working within the constraints of the winapi. Any suggestions?

It prints the stacktraces to stderr/out so I think you can capture them just fine. The bigger problem is making it crash. I know it's sigstop on unix, no idea what it is in windows. Worst case we can add a crash/debug endpoint which returns the stacktraces as json or forces a panic.
Hmm, I can't seem to find anything helpful online.
See http://stackoverflow.com/a/19145992/1508606 and STPROFILER
Perfect, thanks :+1:

body: Also, STTRACE=sync (I think) will log lock usage, there is also another var (check help) for defining a threshold what gets logged. Hard to find links on the phone.

Ok, I had several of those crashes (https://github.com/canton7/SyncTrayzor/issues/252) appearing randomly. Usually after prolonged usage (i.e. running ST overnight). 
Now, while the full blown crash is quite rare, the same error message appears in the logs far more frequently.

So, here's SyncTrayzor log with the error, appearing after "wake from sleep":
https://gist.github.com/anonymous/a2baa96d5f17b65c269f36316493b6ed

And, as per canton7's request, I've set `STPROFILER=localhost:8385`, and here's the output of  `http://localhost:8385/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2`: 
https://gist.github.com/anonymous/973b8cbf5cfb9f3cad63daa184403b1a

So the crash you posted now does not look related to the original crash, furthermore, I don't see any reasonable blocking from syncthing. The only lock I can see is on the GetIgnores() due to a scan currently running.
OK, I'll post again the "actual" crash then, once I'll catch it
That SyncTrayzor log doesn't show a crash, no.

I have had SyncTrayzor & Syncthing silently crashing during "wake from sleep", here are the logs:
SyncTrayzor: https://gist.github.com/anonymous/a52a5158bd4cca9145137fda6092dc2d
Syncthing: https://gist.github.com/anonymous/7134dbcbadf381ff1e83961fb7056c31

Unfortunately, `/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2` can't be polled, since syncthing is dead...
This is on Synctrayzors plate, not syncthings.
Yes, this is a separate issue. Please open a new issue on SyncTrayzor's issue tracker.
Any reproducers, or should we close this?

I added some logs here recently: https://github.com/canton7/SyncTrayzor/issues/252#issuecomment-226832675

If people are positive that it's purely a wrapper's fault, than this can be closed...
So there are no outstanding/in progress rest requests in the profiles you posted.
If @canton7 confirms that the cause behind those recent crashes isn't due to syncthing's misbehave, we can close this.

The logs of @scienmind's from SyncTrayzor still show `/rest/system/{pause,resume}` hanging for long periods. 

Last I remember, we were waiting for @scienmind to post the output of `/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2` after it happens again.

I can't look up which request they're making since I'm on mobile, but the error is `SocketException No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it 127.0.0.1:PORT` instead of the timeout I opened this issue about.
I'll have a better look tomorrow when I'm at a computer.
